title: Early voting begins Saturday as Hochul, Blakeman make final push in race for NY governor - ABC7 New York

Early voting begins Saturday in New York governor race as Hochul, Blakeman campaign statewide - ABC7 New York

 Early voting begins Saturday as Hochul, Blakeman make final push in race for NY governor 
 Stream New York's #1 news - AccuWeather - original content 24/7 By Phil Taitt Friday, October 23, 2026 8:45AM Share NEW YORK (WABC) -- New Yorkers can start casting ballots Saturday as early voting begins in the race for governor.
 Both candidates are making campaign stops ahead of voting. On Friday, Gov. Kathy Hochul and Mayor Zohran Mamdani are expected to make their first joint campaign appearance in Brooklyn. The two were in the Bronx earlier this week for a childcare announcement, and Hochul is highlighting their partnership as part of her campaign message.
 "As New York's first mom and grandmother governor, childcare is personal to me. That's why I'm proud to work alongside Zohran Mamdani to bring New York one step closer to universal childcare," Hochul said in a social media video.
 Meanwhile, Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman says he's not concerned about Hochul appearing alongside the mayor. In fact, he says the partnership helps his campaign by reminding voters that the governor is aligned with a self-described democratic socialist mayor.
 "The more Zohran Mamdani and Kathy Hochul campaign together, the more likely it is that not only will I have a victory, but an astounding victory," Blakeman said.
 He added: "I hope they are real active together. I think it's a huge boost to my campaign. Thank you to both of them for campaigning together, and keep doing it."
 According to a recent Quinnipiac poll , Hochul holds a 14-point lead over Blakeman. Blakeman disputes the findings, saying polls often undersample Republicans and arguing the race is much closer than the numbers suggest.
 Hochul is expected to cast her early vote in Buffalo on Saturday, marking the start of nine days of early voting before Election Day on Nov. 3.
